newsitem.title: USA: Two dead, two missing in Louisiana well blowout.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, two missing in Louisiana well blowout.

text.p: Two workers were killed and two others missing on Tuesday following an overnight explosion and fire on a natural gas drilling rig in southern Louisiana, officials said.

Eighteen other workers were evacuated after the well blew out, sending flames shooting 200 feet into the air over a marsh in St. Martin Parish about 40 miles (64 kms) southwest of Baton Rouge, La., officials said.
"The natural gas rig Mallard 52 burst into flames that were reaching 200 feet into the sky," U.S. Coast Guard Petty Officer Tyler Johnson said.

The fire was being fueled by 20 million cubic feet of gas per day flowing from the well, and a specialized firefighting crew was being sent to the remote area of inland waters to extinguish the blaze and cap the well.
The well is operated by Denbury Resources Inc., and was being drilled by Mallard Bay Drilling, a subsidiary of Tulsa, Okla.-based Parker Drilling Co., Denbury said in a statement.
There were no reports of environmental damage.
